data.description:
Found while finishing Acetate's ACE-801 (Sentry rollout on the same org).

WHAT HAPPENED. c11's Sentry project was fine. The ORG's quota was not. `stage-11-kl` is on the free Developer plan — 5,000 errors/month, shared across every project — and the retired `demo-project` (id 4511028453900288, retired April 2026) still had an ACTIVE client key. Old c11 builds in the wild kept sending to that retired DSN. Over 30 days it consumed 3,735 of the 5,000 errors and had 1,121,397 more rejected. Its top issues are another user's installs (`c11_cli.CLIError: Socket not found at /Users/<someone-else>/...`) and `App Hanging ... 2000 ms` at a threshold c11 has since changed — entirely stale traffic.

CONSEQUENCE FOR c11: 11,700 error events DROPPED in that window (30d: accepted 1,466, rate_limited 11,700). c11 production error monitoring was effectively blind for at least a week, and nothing surfaced it — quota exhaustion is silent to the sender. Events are accepted at the edge with HTTP 200 and a real event id, then discarded server-side as `outcome=rate_limited`. Only `stats_v2` can see it.

WHAT I DID, 2026-08-04: deactivated `demo-project`'s client key (key id ce836c6e3462a139dcd469f5e4d3ceec, isActive: false). The project is intact, not deleted; one PUT reverses it. c11's own key was verified untouched and active. Full write-up + the two diagnostic curl calls are in platform/sentry.md § 'The quota incident (2026-08-04)'.

WHAT REMAINS (this ticket). Consumed quota is not refundable: the billing period runs to 2026-08-24 with onDemandMaxSpend 0 and no trial left, so the org stays blocked until then and c11 is still blind right now.

  1. After 2026-08-24, confirm c11 events are actually being STORED again — check outcome=accepted, not just that the SDK returns an event id. The whole lesson here is that those two are not the same thing.
  2. Decide the budget question. c11 alone used ~1,466 accepted errors in 30d against a 5,000 org cap, and Acetate is about to become a second reporting client on the same cap. Per-key rate limits do NOT exist on this plan (the `rate-limits` feature is absent from the org — a PUT with a rateLimit body returns null and silently does nothing, verified). So the only fences are a paid plan or an on-demand budget. Billing = operator decision.
  3. Consider whether any shipped c11 build still points at the retired DSN. Deactivating the key means those installs now report nowhere at all — which is strictly better than eating the org's quota, but it is worth knowing if a supported version is affected.
data.title: Sentry error monitoring was blind for a week — verify it resumes after the 2026-08-24 quota reset

data.body:
SENTRY AUDIT 2026-08-04. All three open items now have answers, and one of them was wrong in a way worth recording.

1. QUOTA / PLAN — resolved, better than expected. The org is no longer on Developer. `stage-11-kl` is now Team (`am3_team`): $29/mo for 50,000 errors, `onDemandMaxSpend` 2000 cents shared, `allowOnDemand: true`. The billing period reset to 2026-08-04 -> 2026-09-03 with usage 0, so the org is NOT blocked and does not need to wait for 2026-08-24. Hard monthly ceiling is $49. Verified: categories.errors = {reserved: 50000, usage: 0, usageExceeded: false}.

2. RATE LIMITS — still unavailable, re-verified after the upgrade. Per-key rate limits are a Business feature, not a Team one. `PUT /projects/stage-11-kl/c11/keys/<id>/` with a rateLimit body returns `rateLimit: null` with the user token and 403 with the org token; the spike-protection endpoint is 403 as well. Client-side budgets remain the only fence. This ticket's item 2 assumed a paid plan would provide one; it does not.

3. SHIPPED BUILDS ON THE RETIRED DSN — answered, and the answer was not just old builds. `CLI/c11.swift` on `main` still hard-coded demo-project's DSN (line 65), and the CLI captured a Sentry event on every socket-connect failure and every failed Claude-hook dispatch: one per shell prompt, per agent tool call, per hook. That is the 1,121,397 rejected events. It also ran `sendDefaultPii = true`, which is why another user's absolute home path appeared in an issue title. Repointing that DSN at the live c11 project without a fence would have moved ~1.12M events/month onto the real quota and exhausted 50,000 in roughly 1.3 days.

WHAT c11 ACTUALLY SENDS. On 2026-07-25 (last day before the block) the c11 project accepted 1,848 events. 1,816 of them — 98% — were main-thread-hang warnings from two issues: C11-30 "main thread hang 2335ms" (941 events, 11 users) and C11-31 "main thread hang 10422ms (persist)" (875 events, 7 users). The watchdog re-captures a wedged main thread every 5s and sent every capture, so one beachball produced 720 events/hour while Sentry grouped them into a single issue anyway. Current attempted rate is ~1,343/day (313 rate_limited + 1,030 client_discard in 24h), i.e. ~40k/month against the 50k org quota shared with acetate.

The only fatal-level issue, C11-Z "EXC_BREAKPOINT: Index out of range" (24 events, 5 "users"), is entirely `c11Tests` running under XCTestCore — not a production crash. Sentry was starting in XCTest hosts; PostHog and MainThreadHangMonitor already opted out.

Production release mix over 14d: 1,725 of 1,784 production events came from com.stage11.c11@0.58.0+116 alone.

FIXES LANDED — PR #401 (Stage-11-Agentics/c11):
  - `SentryEventBudget` in beforeSend: 20 events/hour, 50/day per process, of which at most 3/hour and 15/day may be hang reports. Fatal exempt.
  - Hang reports: one per episode, only for episodes >= 5s. Local hang log unchanged.
  - CLI: no compiled-in DSN at all; opt-in via `C11_CLI_SENTRY_DSN`; sendDefaultPii off.
  - Sentry no longer starts under an XCTest host.
  - platform/sentry.md updated (Team plan, $49 ceiling, client-side-only fence table, the CLI as the real 1.12M source).

Expected effect on 2026-07-25's traffic: 1,848 events -> under ~150, with every distinct issue still represented.

REMAINING FOR THIS TICKET. Only the verification half is left, and the date moved: after PR #401 ships in a release, confirm via stats_v2 that c11 events are `accepted` (not merely returning an event id) and that the monthly accepted total lands in the low thousands rather than ~40k. The underlying hangs now have their own tickets: C11-191 (tab bar preference pass, 2.3s) and C11-192 (SwiftUI Button generic metadata, 10s).

data.body:
REAL-ARTIFACT VALIDATION 2026-08-04. The throttle works, and running it found a defect that the seven green unit tests could not.

WHAT WAS RUN. Tagged `c11-190` build (reload.sh, operator-approved), launched directly so stdout was captured, main thread wedged from outside the process with lldb — `+[NSThread sleepUntilDate:]` enqueued on the main queue, then detach. A genuine beachball as far as the watchdog is concerned; no test seam added to the app. 23 episodes on the merged code, 17 on the fixed code.

THE DEFECT. The global ceiling was charged twice for every hang report. `MainThreadHangMonitor` consulted `SentryEventBudgetGate` before capturing, then `beforeSend` consulted it again for the same event and classified it `.other`, because it only inspected the level. Three hang reports spent six of the twenty hourly slots. Measured on the running build, the ceiling behaved as 17 events/hour rather than the documented 20. It fails safe — the fence held, nothing escaped — but the shortfall grows with how much the app is hanging, which is precisely when the remaining allowance matters. Fixed in PR #404: the budget is consulted in exactly one place, `beforeSend`, classifying by level (fatal exempt) and by the `category` tag the hang path already sets; the watchdog keeps its shape filters and no longer touches the budget.

WHAT THE THROTTLE ACTUALLY DID.
  - 23 episodes produced 67 local captures in the hang log and 3 outbound hang warnings — exactly the 3/hour cap. One episode of ~24s: 3 captures, 1 event, HTTP 200.
  - A real 2,882 ms episode produced local captures and zero outbound attempts. The 5s floor holds.
  - After the fix, suppression is 1 attempt per episode instead of 3, so `sentrySuppressed=` in the hang log now counts episodes rather than recaptures.
  - After the fix, 19 non-fatal events were allowed with none refused, where the merged code began refusing at 17.

STARTUP IS FINE. `SDK initialized! Version: 9.3.0` with the HTTP transport created, on both builds. `beforeSend` was added to a startup path, so this was checked rather than assumed.

CRASHES ARE STILL EXEMPT, READ BACK FROM THE SERVER. SIGABRT on the tagged build, relaunch, crash report flushed: `level = fatal`, mechanism `signal/SIGABRT`, HTTP 200, and event `96cb1c971b6245889b891058332adcaf` confirmed STORED via the API with a `dateReceived`. Not an event id from the SDK — the thing the SDK cannot tell you. One honest limit: a crash ends the process, so a crash report is always sent from a fresh process with an empty budget; the exhausted-budget-plus-crash case is covered by unit test, not by the artifact.

ITEM 1 OF THIS TICKET IS ANSWERED. The org's billing period reset on 2026-08-04 (Team, 50,000/mo) and c11 events are being accepted again. Bracketing `stats_v2` in one-hour windows: the last hour shows `accepted` and zero `rate_limited`, where the preceding hours were entirely `rate_limited/error_usage_exceeded`. Nothing is waiting on 2026-08-24.

THE ONGOING CHECK. `scripts/telemetry/sentry-position.py` (in #404) prints the quota position and a per-project accepted / client_discard / rate_limited table with drop reasons, and exits non-zero when events are being dropped, so it is a check and not just a report. `platform/sentry.md` points at it and records the two joins that bite; committed there as 9782d7c and pushed.

STILL OPEN, FOR WHOEVER PICKS THIS UP. After a release ships with 42ce4c919 plus #404, confirm via `stats_v2` that c11 events are `accepted` and that the monthly accepted total lands in the low thousands rather than the ~40k/month the project was on track for. The shipped 0.58.0 build is visible in the same data still doing the old thing — roughly 60 events/hour, sub-5s hangs and every persist recapture — which is both the baseline and the reason the release matters.

BUDGET NUMBERS NOT TOUCHED. 20/hour, 50/day, 3 and 15 for hangs are unchanged. The measurement said the arithmetic was wrong, not the policy.

SECOND DEFECT, found while validating: dSYM uploads have never landed.

The auto-fired plan review flagged that `release.yml` and `nightly.yml` set `SENTRY_PROJECT: stage11-c11` while the slug is `c11`. Checked, and it is worse than "may be landing in the wrong project": `GET /projects/stage-11-kl/stage11-c11/` returns 404, no such project exists, and the real `c11` project has ZERO debug files. Every dSYM upload since the integration landed has gone nowhere. The step carries `continue-on-error: true`, so it failed silently every time — the same shape as the quota incident this ticket exists for: monitoring that looks wired and is not. The practical cost is that production c11 crash stacks on Sentry are unsymbolicated, which is most of what a crash report is for.

One-token fix in both workflows, in PR #404. Verify after the next release ships:

    curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SENTRY_USER_AUTH_TOKEN" \
      https://sentry.io/api/0/projects/stage-11-kl/c11/files/dsyms/

On the plan review's six operator calls: item (4)'s hang double-charge is the defect I found and fixed independently — see the validation comment above and #404. The other five (release vehicle for #401, recurrence detector, IP/geo posture, c11's declared share of the 50k pool, demo-project key delete-vs-deactivate) are operator decisions and are left as flagged; none of them blocked the validation, which is done.

REBASED ONTO #402, AND RE-VALIDATED ON THE REBASED TREE.

The PR sat CONFLICTING, which on this repo silently suppresses the real CI — only the Drawbridge jobs ran and the `build` gate never fired at all. Rebased onto origin/main (now carrying #402, C11-192's hang fingerprinting), resolved the one real conflict in `MainThreadHangMonitor.reportTelemetry`, and CI came alive: `build` passes in 6m21s, so the new unit tests are green.

The rebase mattered for more than mergeability. #402 rewrote the hang report path underneath this work — new message text, a fingerprint, and a `tags:` parameter carrying `hang.cause` / `hang.culprit` / `hang.top_symbol`. My classifier keys on the `category` tag, so a tags rewrite is exactly the kind of change that could have quietly broken it. Rebuilt and re-ran on the rebased tree:

  - `category = hang` still arrives at `beforeSend`, sitting alongside #402's new `hang.*` tags. Confirmed by reading the serialized event off the running process.
  - 6 episodes, 13 local captures, exactly 3 outbound hang events — the 3/hour cap — then 1 suppressed attempt per episode.
  - Sentry still initializes on the rebased build.

So the validated claim now holds against what is actually in the PR, not only against the tree I first measured.

Worth recording as a repo-level lesson, since it cost a full CI cycle to notice: a CONFLICTING c11 PR still shows a wall of green Drawbridge checks while the job that actually compiles and runs tests never starts. Green Drawbridge with no `build` row means "CI did not run", not "CI passed". Check `mergeStateStatus` before believing a green PR.

MERGED as b16cdb3a7 (PR #404, squash). All 10 CI checks green including the build gate and compat-tests. Both defects are on main: the global budget double-charge, and the dSYM uploads pointing at a project that does not exist.

Ticket work is complete. What remains is not doable until a release ships: confirm via stats_v2 that c11 events are accepted and the monthly total lands in the low thousands rather than ~40k, and confirm dSYMs actually appear on the c11 project (curl .../projects/stage-11-kl/c11/files/dsyms/ — it is empty today). Both are one command each; sentry-position.py covers the first.

The plan review's NEEDS HUMAN still stands for the five operator calls I did not take: the release vehicle for #401+#404, a recurrence detector, the c11 project's IP/geo posture, c11's declared share of the 50k org pool, and demo-project key delete-vs-deactivate.

Code review: PR #404 went through the repo's Drawbridge lane — drawbridge-gate, drawbridge-review and drawbridge-judge all passed — alongside the full CI suite (build, compat-tests, remote-daemon-tests, workflow-guard-tests, web-typecheck, build-ghosttykit). Merged as b16cdb3a7.

Beyond the automated review, the substantive check on this change was the real-artifact run rather than the diff: the fix was derived from a measurement on a running build, and re-measured on a rebuilt binary after rebasing onto #402. The failure it corrects was invisible to seven passing unit tests, which is the argument for having run it at all.

Status set to BLOCKED, not done, deliberately. Every part of this ticket that can be executed now has been: the throttle is proven on a real artifact, two defects found and fixed on main, and the org's position is readable on demand. What is left is the ticket's own headline — confirm c11 events are stored and bounded once the fix ships — and that is unrunnable until a release carries 42ce4c919 + b16cdb3a7. The unblocking move is operator call (1) from the plan review: cherry-pick onto release/v0.63.0, or wait for v0.64.0.

When it ships, two commands close this out:
  code/c11/scripts/telemetry/sentry-position.py --period 24h
  curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $SENTRY_USER_AUTH_TOKEN" https://sentry.io/api/0/projects/stage-11-kl/c11/files/dsyms/
